newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Five U.N. staff said held hostage in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Five U.N. staff said held hostage in Tajikistan.

text.p: Four U.N. military observers and their interpreter were taken hostage on Tuesday by a breakaway Tajik rebel group near an area where a similar incident occurred in December, a U.N. spokesman said.
Two of the observers were from Switzerland and one each from Austria and Ukraine, the spokesman said.

They were seized along with their local interpreter by armed followers of Rizvon Saidov, a guerrilla commander who was once allied to the Islamic rebel opposition to President Imomali Rakhmonov but who later switched back to supporting the government while retaining control of his own supporters.

The captors were demanding safe passage for their members into Tajikistan from Afghanistan, where many anti-goverenment guerrillas are based. The United Nations has demanded the hostages' immediate release.

Tens of thousands of people have been killed in a four-year civil war between the secular government and Islamist guerrillas. About 45 U.N. military observers are stationed in the country where the Russian-led Commonwealth of Independent States has a much larger peacekeeping force.
The U.N. staff members were seized 2.5 miles (4 kms) southwest of Obigarm, between Garm and Dushanbe, the capital, the U.N. spokesman said.

The so-called Rizvon group seized 23 people including seven U.N. observers and two local staff in December. The group then demanded the Islamic opposition release Saidov's brother and three other people in exchange for the hostages.

All the hostages were released the next day except for two rebel members of a joint commission, who were exchanged on Dec. 26 for two of the four people whose release the Rizvon group had demanded. Of the other two, one was found to have been released some time earlier and the other had died.
